title: Ayodhya's 10th Deepotsav Lights Over 30 Lakh Diyas Across 56 Saryu Ghats
headline: Ayodhya's 10th Deepotsav Lights Over 30 Lakh Diyas Across 56 Saryu Ghats
subheadline: Reports from the night put the count above 30 lakh lamps — The Hindu's headline said over 36 lakh — with the official Guinness tally still awaited against 2025's 26.17 lakh record.
summary: Reports from the night put the count above 30 lakh lamps — The Hindu's headline said over 36 lakh — with the official Guinness tally still awaited against 2025's 26.17 lakh record.

body:
• More than 30 lakh earthen lamps were lit across 56 ghats along the Saryu in Ayodhya on Saturday, November 7, for the 10th Deepotsav, PTI and the New Indian Express reported; The Hindu's video headline put the figure at over 36 lakh.
  • No Guinness World Records adjudicator's count appeared in the reports read on the night, so the official total is not yet certified; the 2025 record stood at 26.17 lakh lamps.
  • Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan was chief guest, alongside Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.
  • More than 35,000 volunteers lit the lamps, and a 2,100-drone show recreated scenes from the Ramayana over the riverfront.

Ayodhya lit more than 30 lakh earthen lamps across 56 ghats along the Saryu river on Saturday, November 7, as the 10th Deepotsav reached its main night on the eve of Diwali, PTI and the New Indian Express reported. The Hindu's video coverage headlined the figure at over 36 lakh diyas. The counts reported on the night differ, and no report read by late Saturday carried a final tally announced by a Guinness World Records adjudicator or the Uttar Pradesh government.

What was planned, what was reported

Organisers had set a target of 30 lakh diyas for this year and procured about 33 lakh lamps through Dr Rammanohar Lohia Avadh University, which coordinated the arrangements, to allow for breakage in transport and placement. More than 35,000 volunteers, drawn from the university and local colleges, laid out and lit the lamps along the riverfront, including the expanded Ram Ki Paidi. Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan attended as chief guest, with Governor Anandiben Patel and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, according to the reports compiled by NewsPlainly from PTI and New Indian Express coverage. A fleet of 2,100 drones recreated scenes from the Ramayana above the Saryu as part of the evening's programme.

The record question

The diya count is the number Ayodhya uses to claim world records, which is why the distinction between a reported count and a certified one matters. In 2024, a Guinness adjudicator announced the count on the evening itself — 25,12,585 lamps, counted with drones. The 2025 record was 26.17 lakh. If the reported figure above 30 lakh is confirmed, this year's display would clear the 2025 mark by more than 3.8 lakh lamps; until the official count is announced, that remains a reported figure, not a certified record.

Ten years of Deepotsav

Deepotsav began in 2017 with about 1.71 lakh lamps. A decade on, the festival runs for several days around Diwali with Ramlila performances, sand art, projection mapping and fireworks alongside the main lighting, and the ghat footprint has grown from 55 ghats to 56. The 2026 celebrations were scheduled from November 5 to November 9. For the diaspora reader, the verified position is this: the 10th Deepotsav happened on Saturday night at a scale above 30 lakh lamps by every count reported, and the one number still awaited is the official tally that would settle the record.
